summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image based on Ubuntu that runs an SSH server. It installs OpenSSH, creates a test user account with a password, configures SSH settings to allow password-based login while blocking root access, and then starts the SSH server when the container runs.

explanations.5: The backslash at the end of the line allows the RUN command to continue on the next line, keeping related commands grouped together logically.
explanations.7: apt-get clean removes package cache files to reduce the image size, since once packages are installed, the cached downloads aren't needed anymore.
explanations.8: This removes the apt package lists to further shrink the image; since packages are already installed, these lists would just waste disk space.
explanations.12: useradd creates a new user account; the flags set the home directory to /home/christophe and the shell to /bin/bash so the user can log in and use the terminal.
explanations.13: This pipes the username and password through chpasswd, which is a tool designed specifically to set passwords for user accounts in a script.
explanations.16: sed is a text editor that finds and replaces patterns in files; here it's disabling root login by uncommenting and setting PermitRootLogin to 'no' in the SSH config file.
explanations.23: EXPOSE tells Docker which port this container listens on, though it doesn't actually open the port—that happens when you run the container with the right flags.
explanations.25: CMD specifies what command runs when the container starts; the -D flag tells sshd to run in the foreground so Docker can see it running and keep the container alive.
